PCB design in KiCad

CUSTOM HARDWARE

Bike Navigation PCB

A custom two-layer PCB intended as the electronics platform for a bike-navigation device. The ESP32-S3 runs the firmware and coordinates the user interface; the 2.4-inch TFT touch display provides visual interaction; the TP4056 USB-C module charges the Li-Po battery; the XL6009 boost converter provides a higher supply rail where required; and the MAX98357A I²S amplifier drives a speaker for spoken prompts. The INMP441 I²S microphone supports audio input, while a slide switch provides power control. Route guidance and location tracking require suitable location hardware and firmware; those functions should not be claimed as complete until tested.

Key components: ESP32-S3 Mini (ESP32-S3FH4R2), 2.4-inch TFT touch display, TP4056 USB-C Li-Po charger, 2600 mAh Li-Po battery, XL6009 boost converter, MAX98357A I²S audio amplifier, INMP441 I²S microphone, and slide switch.

  • KiCad
  • ESP32-S3
  • TFT touch display
  • TP4056
  • XL6009
  • MAX98357A
  • INMP441

CONTROLLER BOARD

Desk Buddy PCB

A custom KiCad PCB intended to act as the controller board for a desk companion device. The microcontroller (as identified in the schematic) would coordinate connected inputs and outputs, while the PCB provides the power and signal connections between those parts. The schematic explains electrical connectivity, the layout shows component placement and copper routing, and the board render shows the physical arrangement. The exact component list and functions must be taken from the Desk Buddy schematic/BOM; I have not added unverified part numbers or features.

Components used: Refer to the Desk Buddy schematic and bill of materials (BOM) for the exact microcontroller, power components, inputs, outputs, and connectors. I have left the part-level list unspecified rather than guessing component names from the image filenames.

  • KiCad
  • Schematic capture
  • PCB layout
  • 3D board view
